svg.title: Factory Method
svg.desc: Factory Method. Let subclasses decide which class to create: the base class codes against an interface and calls an overridable create method. Step 1, new inside send(): send() picks the channel with if/else, so Notifier knows every channel and push means another edit. Step 2, Defer to createChannel(): send() calls createChannel() and talks only to Channel; each subclass returns its own channel. Step 3, One call at runtime: send() runs in the base class; createChannel() runs in SmsNotifier and returns a new SmsChannel. Step 4, New channel, no edits: Push adds two classes and edits none: send() is untouched. The cost: a creator subclass per product.

g.text: send() picks the channel with if/else, so Notifier knows every channel and push means another edit.
send() calls createChannel() and talks only to Channel; each subclass returns its own channel.
send() runs in the base class; createChannel() runs in SmsNotifier and returns a new SmsChannel.
Push adds two classes and edits none: send() is untouched. The cost: a creator subclass per product.
// written once: no if/else, no concrete class
Notifier depends on every concrete channel: each new one means editing send() again
Cost one creator subclass per product, which is why many languages pass a factory function instead
